text:
incident-bot: ALERT: gpu-pool-nyc queue length > 12k, avg token latency > 2.4s, autoscaler errors observed :rotating_light:
kevin: i'm on it, paging oncall. seeing spike from /v1/generate - lots of long-seq requests
dalia: noticed continuous-batcher config rolled 10m ago (max_batch_tokens=4096 -> 8192). suspect longer hold windows + larger kv cache churn
samir: also seeing a flurry of prefix-cache misses across pods, eviction rate spiked. logs: `kvcache.evictions/sec 1200`
kevin: autoscaler logs show repeated leader election timeouts and failed scaling decisions: `error: scale lock timeout`
ops-bot: Pager sent to @kevin, escalation policy: SRE -> eng-runtime -> eng-infra
kevin: quick ask: can we temporarily throttle incoming generation concurrency per-tenant? want immediate relief while rolling back batch params
dalia: yes, we can flip per-route concurrency cap via config-service. running: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/_config/route/throttle -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","max_concurrency":50}'`
samir: running a one-off to revert the continuous-batcher change now. `kubectl patch config continuous-batcher --patch '{"spec":{"max_batch_tokens":4096}}'`
jules: heads-up: this will reduce throughput but should cut average latency and reduce kv churn
kevin: done: concurrency cap applied. traffic dropped ~30% at edge within 40s. queue length declining slowly
dalia: autoscaler still stuck. digging deeper into leader election logs. looks like lease controller failed to renew due to a GC pause in controller-manager on the autoscale leader node
samir: i can manual scale cluster to add 4 gpus as short-term. will also enable model-fallback to smaller variant (gpt-small-latency) for heavy tenants to lower token work
kevin: please proceed. notify customers with impacted SLAs once we have stability metrics
ops-bot: manual scale triggered by samir: `redwoodctl capacity add --pool gpu-pool-nyc --count 4 --reason "incident 2178881234 manual scale"`
samir: scale accepted but new nodes are scheduling slowly because kube-scheduler had extant taints from earlier maintenance. removing taints on the two pending nodes now
dalia: while nodes come up, i'm going to force leader re-election on autoscaler to break the lock: `kubectl delete pod -l app=autoscaler -n redwood-system` — will cause a brief control-plane blip
mia: ok keep me posted. i'll draft a short customer note: "We observed elevated latencies due to autoscaling delays and a batching config regression; mitigations in progress."
kevin: autoscaler pods recycled -> new leader elected. controllers report successful scale decisions, new GPUs joining pool
samir: nodes ready; scaled pool capacity +4. batch revert rolled back earlier. prefix-cache hits improving: `kvcache.hit_ratio` from 0.42 -> 0.78 over the last 3m
jules: queue length back to normal. token latency sliding down to normal SLOs
kevin: handing to SRE for post-incident work and root-cause. leaving the channel for documentation. @dalia take lead on RCA
dalia: taking handoff. immediate action items: 1) revert continuous-batcher change (done) 2) add guardrail to prevent batch param increases without canary 3) fix autoscaler leader election robustness and increase lease renewal deadline 4) update alerts to include increasing kvcache.evictions as an early signal
dalia: initial customer impact estimate: 18 customers saw >25% request throttling for ~12 minutes, 4 customers experienced degraded p99 latency above SLA, no data exfiltration or model correctness regressions identified
kevin: filing a follow-up incident report and scheduling a postmortem tomorrow 10:00am PT. tagging eng-runtime, eng-sre, product, and support
incident-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2178881234. Severity: sev2. Postmortem owner: dalia.
mia: i'll coordinate customer comms post-postmortem. draft will note mitigations: throttle, manual scale, revert, leader-restart
dalia: saving logs and config diffs, attaching to the incident. will include timeline and runbook changes
kevin: thanks everyone. closing the live page. please add any residual notes here for the postmortem
samir: note for RCA: the rollback validation step was flaky in the CI job that deploys batcher configs -> will open a PR to add a canary check and automated rollback trigger
jules: also recommend a temporary autoscale policy: allow 10% burst headroom from reserved capacity to absorb sudden surges
dalia: ack. will add to action list and track in INC ticket
kevin: thanks. :thumbsup:
